newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia-Pacific nations worried by U.S. telecom rates.
newsitem.headline: Asia-Pacific nations worried by U.S. telecom rates.

text.p: A group of Asian Pacific nations called on the International Telecommunications Union (ITU) on Saturday to study the impact of the U.S. global telecom accounting rates on Asia's developing countries.

The group, which includes Tonga, Papua New Guinea, Nauru and Western Samoa, urged that the ITU to study carefully the financial and economic implications of global accounting rates declared by U.S. regulators last year.
It said the ITU should decide if the rates are "fair to the telecom operators of the Asia Pacific region".

The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) announced last December that Washington would cut its accounting rates paid to foreign telecom operators to complete international calls, sparking protests around the world.
"You need a consensus. You can't impose certain rates on somebody," a delegate from the group said at the Asia Telecom 97 conference in Singapore. "It's like declaring a war."
The group said the ITU should also study a scheme to share the revenues earned from call back services among telecommunication operators.
Call-back services, which route call through the U.S. to take advantage of lower prices there, have sharply trimmed the profits of Asian telecommunication operators, they said.
